SQLQueryBuilder.select:
[DEFINE_WORKER: "Builds and returns a SELECT SQL query string for a given table, optionally projecting specific columns and filtering rows with equality conditions joined by AND." select]
    [INPUTS]
        <REF> table </REF>: string "The name of the database table to query"
        <REF> columns </REF>: string or list of strings "The columns to select; defaults to '*' meaning all columns; if a list is provided each element is a column name"
        <REF> where </REF>: dict or None "Optional mapping of column names to equality filter values; if None or empty no WHERE clause is added"
    [END_INPUTS]

    [OUTPUTS]
        <REF> query </REF>: string "The fully assembled SQL SELECT statement as a plain string"
    [END_OUTPUTS]

    [MAIN_FLOW]
        [SEQUENTIAL_BLOCK]
            [COMMAND Check whether columns is not equal to the sentinel string '*'; if it is not, join all elements of the columns list into a single comma-separated string and overwrite the columns variable with that string RESULT columns]
            [COMMAND Construct the base query string by interpolating the columns string and table name into the template 'SELECT {columns} FROM {table}'; note that neither columns nor table is validated or escaped at this point, creating a potential SQL injection vector if either originates from external input RESULT query]
            [COMMAND Check whether where is truthy (non-None and non-empty); if so, build a WHERE clause by formatting each key-value pair from where as "{k}='{v}'", joining all pairs with ' AND ', prepending ' WHERE ', and appending the result to query RESULT query]
            [COMMAND Return the fully assembled query string RESULT query]
        [END_SEQUENTIAL_BLOCK]
    [END_MAIN_FLOW]

    [ALTERNATIVE_FLOW: columns equals '*' on entry]
        [SEQUENTIAL_BLOCK]
            [COMMAND Skip the join step and keep columns as the literal string '*', so the SELECT clause becomes 'SELECT * FROM {table}' RESULT columns]
        [END_SEQUENTIAL_BLOCK]
    [END_ALTERNATIVE_FLOW]

    [ALTERNATIVE_FLOW: where is None or evaluates to falsy]
        [SEQUENTIAL_BLOCK]
            [COMMAND Skip the WHERE clause construction and return the base 'SELECT {columns} FROM {table}' string without any filtering predicate RESULT query]
        [END_SEQUENTIAL_BLOCK]
    [END_ALTERNATIVE_FLOW]

[END_WORKER]
SQLQueryBuilder.insert:
[DEFINE_WORKER: "Builds and returns a SQL INSERT statement string for a given table by joining the keys and single-quoted values from a dictionary." insert]
    [INPUTS]
        <REF> table </REF>: string "Name of the target database table"
        <REF> data </REF>: dict "Dictionary mapping column names to their corresponding values"
    [END_INPUTS]

    [OUTPUTS]
        <REF> result </REF>: string "A SQL INSERT INTO statement with columns and single-quoted values derived from the input dictionary"
    [END_OUTPUTS]

    [MAIN_FLOW]
        [SEQUENTIAL_BLOCK]
            [COMMAND Join all keys of data with ', ' as the column list RESULT keys]
            [COMMAND Join all values of data, each wrapped in single quotes, with ', ' as the value list RESULT values]
            [COMMAND Format and return the string 'INSERT INTO {table} ({keys}) VALUES ({values})' using the resolved table name, keys, and values RESULT sql_statement]
        [END_SEQUENTIAL_BLOCK]
    [END_MAIN_FLOW]

[END_WORKER]
SQLQueryBuilder.delete:
[DEFINE_WORKER: "Builds and returns a DELETE SQL query string for a given table, optionally appending a WHERE clause constructed from a dictionary of column-value conditions joined by AND." delete]
    [INPUTS]
        <REF> table </REF>: string "Name of the database table to delete from; interpolated directly into the SQL string with no escaping or validation"
        <REF> where </REF>: dict or None "Optional mapping of column names to values used to build the WHERE clause; defaults to None, in which case no WHERE clause is added"
    [END_INPUTS]

    [OUTPUTS]
        <REF> query </REF>: string "The fully constructed DELETE SQL query string"
    [END_OUTPUTS]

    [MAIN_FLOW]
        [SEQUENTIAL_BLOCK]
            [COMMAND Interpolate table into the string literal 'DELETE FROM ' to produce the base query string and assign it to query RESULT query]
            [COMMAND Evaluate whether where is truthy (non-None and non-empty); if true, proceed to the alternative flow to append the WHERE clause RESULT where_condition]
            [COMMAND Return query RESULT query]
        [END_SEQUENTIAL_BLOCK]
    [END_MAIN_FLOW]

    [ALTERNATIVE_FLOW: where is provided and evaluates as truthy (non-None, non-empty dict)]
        [SEQUENTIAL_BLOCK]
            [COMMAND For each key-value pair (k, v) in where.items(), format each as the string "k='v'" using f-string interpolation with no escaping on either k or v RESULT condition_parts]
            [COMMAND Join all condition_parts with ' AND ' as the separator to produce a single conditions string RESULT conditions_string]
            [COMMAND Append the string ' WHERE ' concatenated with conditions_string to query using in-place string concatenation (+=) RESULT query]
        [END_SEQUENTIAL_BLOCK]
    [END_ALTERNATIVE_FLOW]

[END_WORKER]
SQLQueryBuilder.update:
[DEFINE_WORKER: "Builds a raw SQL UPDATE statement string by interpolating the table name, a SET clause from all key-value pairs in data, and an optional WHERE clause from a separate conditions dict." update]
    [INPUTS]
        <REF> table </REF>: str "Name of the database table to update; used verbatim with no sanitization"
        <REF> data </REF>: dict "Mapping of column names to their new values; must be non-empty to produce valid SQL"
        <REF> where </REF>: dict or None "Optional mapping of column names to filter values; when omitted or None the WHERE clause is skipped"
    [END_INPUTS]

    [OUTPUTS]
        <REF> query </REF>: str "Raw SQL UPDATE string, e.g. 'UPDATE t SET k='v' WHERE k2='v2''; not parameterized and unsafe for untrusted input"
    [END_OUTPUTS]

    [MAIN_FLOW]
        [SEQUENTIAL_BLOCK]
            [COMMAND Iterate over every key-value pair in data; for each pair format it as the string "k='v'" (key unquoted, value wrapped in single quotes); join all resulting strings with ", " as separator and assign the result to update_str RESULT update_str]
            [COMMAND Construct the initial query string by concatenating the literal tokens "UPDATE ", table, " SET ", and update_str using an f-string, then assign it to query RESULT query]
            [COMMAND Return query RESULT query]
        [END_SEQUENTIAL_BLOCK]
    [END_MAIN_FLOW]

    [ALTERNATIVE_FLOW: where is provided and is truthy (non-None, non-empty dict)]
        [SEQUENTIAL_BLOCK]
            [COMMAND Iterate over every key-value pair in where; for each pair format it as the string "k='v'"; join all resulting strings with " AND " as separator to form a WHERE predicate string RESULT where_clause]
            [COMMAND Append the string " WHERE " concatenated with where_clause to query in-place before returning RESULT query]
        [END_SEQUENTIAL_BLOCK]
    [END_ALTERNATIVE_FLOW]

[END_WORKER]
